active_family: 614a native joint38 AR Gaussian likelihood transition law
current_bottleneck: Likelihood training changes the failure mode in a useful way but plain Gaussian innovations are too diffuse and too smooth. 614a passes conditionality, cointegration, cross-cell correlation, and persistent severe undercoverage, but fails surface, distributional fidelity, time-series tails, mean reversion, and pathwise realism. The core issue is no longer only undercoverage; it is over-diffuse Gaussian sampling and poor level/tail shape.
last_result_summary: 614a implemented a conditional likelihood-trained AR transition law over the same generic joint38 empirical-score panel, with full-covariance Gaussian one-step increments and exact NLL. Focused tests passed (2 passed). Training overfit after epoch 2; best val NLL was 15.682419. Official 441-window/48-sample IV bridge scored 4/11: passed conditionality, block-AR, cointegration, cross-cell correlation; failed surface, coverage, time_series, regime_coverage, distributional_fidelity, mean_reversion, pathwise_jump_realism. Key metrics: cov90 90.9%, conditional MAE reduction 6.7%, turb/calm width 0.926, persistent severe undercoverage 4.0% pass, regime layer2 0/8, daily KS 12/25, level KS 0/25, median-bias cells 8/25, bad windows 0%, kurtosis ratio 0.305, cointegration gen/GT 0.766, cross-cell corr/rank 0.822/1.611, mean-reversion ratio 0.304, pathwise KS 0.646, q99 jump-scale cells 6/25.
next_step_recommendation: Keep the likelihood-trained AR transition paradigm alive but do not ship 614a. Run a controlled sampler-temperature diagnostic on 614a to determine whether its main pathology is over-diffuse Gaussian sampling. If moderate down-temperature restores distribution/time-series/mean-reversion realism while preserving coverage and persistent-undercoverage gains, continue NLL calibration; otherwise move to a heavier-tailed or mixture likelihood family.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 510a, 596a, and 610a all score 5/11. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product but is a composed deck, not a calibrated joint law. 610a is the cleanest native joint learned law so far because it generates IV and anchor factors through one shared AR transition model.
